conflict: NYC DOE's own Mayor's Management Report and Wikipedia both confirm charter-school students are counted separately from DOE enrollment (119,551 charter students as of Oct 2018, a figure that has grown substantially since). Colorado's 870,793 figure is a single statewide count that includes charter and pre-K students. Adding NYC's charter enrollment (now well over 150,000) to the 793,300 DOE figure would push NYC's total public-school population past 900,000 -- likely exceeding Colorado's count rather than trailing it.
finding: The two sides are not counted the same way. NYC's number is DOE district schools only, excluding roughly 150,000+ charter-school students that Colorado's statewide total does include, and possibly excluding some pre-K enrollment as well. On a consistent definition (all public school students, any type), New York City likely has MORE students than Colorado, not fewer -- the opposite of what the sentence implies.
